Triggers.value: Being in a locked or confined room
Being in a natural environment similar to where it happened

Threat.value: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

Memory.value: When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once
Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning

Negative Appraisals.value: I have lost my faith in people, life, or a higher power
My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe
I can't stop bad things from happening to me

issues.explanation: Threat items imply an ongoing personal-danger/being-followed formulation, which is hard to reconcile with trauma to a loved one; they read more like direct interpersonal victimization than fear for a loved one.

Within Threat, 'Checking Behind' and 'Avoid Unfamiliar Places' reflect hypervigilant danger avoidance, while 'Risky Behavior' points in the opposite direction behaviorally; this combination is possible but clinically strained without any other items supporting disinhibition.

Memory item 'Pain Recall' implies bodily re-experiencing of injury to the patient's own body, which is difficult to fit with trauma to a loved one unless she was also directly harmed; the other memory items do not suggest that.

issues.item: Threat: Risky Behavior: Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
issues.explanation: For trauma to a loved one, a prominent risky-behavior item is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile, which is dominated by fear/avoidance and reliving rather than self-endangering behavior. It pulls the threat profile in a different direction without support from other nodes.

issues.item: Memory: Pain Recall: When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
issues.explanation: Pain recall in the same body parts as during the event implies the patient personally sustained bodily injury during the trauma. That is difficult to fit with trauma to a loved one, especially given no other items indicate direct physical victimization.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Body Unreliable: I can no longer trust my own body
issues.explanation: The body-focused negative appraisals suggest distrust of one's own injured or trauma-reactive body, which fits direct bodily trauma better than trauma centered on harm to a loved one. In this profile they are not well supported by the trauma type or the other selected items.

issues.item: Triggers: Military Topics: Talks about military
issues.explanation: For trauma to a loved one, 'military topics' is hard to justify unless the loved one’s trauma was specifically military-related; that context is not represented anywhere else in the profile, so this trigger appears mismatched to the stated trauma type.

issues.item: Triggers: Locked Spaces: Being in a locked or confined room
issues.explanation: 'Locked spaces' suggests a confinement/entrapment trauma context, but the rest of the profile centers on reliving, terror, and generalized danger after trauma to a loved one rather than a personal entrapment event. Without corroborating memory or appraisal content, this trigger looks clinically out of place.

vignette: Sara, a 63-year-old Middle Eastern woman who works as an auditor, has been grappling with intense psychological distress following a traumatic event that involved her loved one. Sara's life changed irrevocably on the day she received news of her nephew's tragic death in a hiking accident. The incident occurred in a remote forest where she and her family often went to spend weekends together. The memory of that day remains vivid and overwhelming for Sara, each detail etched into her mind with the clarity of a full sensory experience. Every time she recalls the event, it feels as though she is reliving every moment-she can hear the rustling of leaves, feel the chill in the air, and see the desolate forest path leading to where her nephew was found. The terror she felt that day comes rushing back whenever something triggers the memory, often without warning. Sara's triggers are particularly potent due to their direct connection to the traumatic event. Being in a natural environment similar to where it happened can instantly bring back the full memory, leaving her feeling as if she is right there again. This has led her to avoid such environments altogether. Moreover, being in locked or confined spaces, like an office or any enclosed room, also triggers her memories and sends waves of anxiety through her. Her hypervigilance is a constant presence, making her superalert and watchful wherever she goes. She cannot shake the feeling that danger lurks around every corner, especially when she ventures into unfamiliar places. This fear has led her to avoid such environments entirely, confining herself to familiar settings where she feels safer. However, this avoidance has had significant consequences on both her personal life and career as an auditor. Sara's sleep problems have also intensified over time. She often finds it difficult to fall asleep or stay asleep due to the intrusive thoughts and memories that keep her mind racing late into the night. Her body remains in a state of high alert even when she is physically safe, reacting as if she were still in danger. This has left her feeling increasingly helpless and unable to prevent bad things from happening. The loss of faith in people, life, and a higher power has compounded Sara's distress. She feels that the world is an unpredictable and dangerous place where no one can be trusted or relied upon for support. Her body's persistent reaction as if she were still in danger further reinforces her sense of helplessness and mistrust. Over the past few months, these symptoms have gradually eroded Sara's ability to function effectively at work. She has become increasingly isolated, avoiding social interactions and professional engagements that could trigger memories or anxiety. Her relationships with colleagues have also suffered as a result of her withdrawal and inability to fully engage in her duties. It was her sister's persistent urging that finally brought Sara to seek help. Her sister recognized the depth of Sara's distress and urged her to speak with someone who could provide support and guidance through this difficult time. Sara is most afraid of losing control and being unable to manage her reactions, but she also hopes for a sense of peace and stability in her life once again. In her current state, Sara feels overwhelmed by the fear that bad things will continue to happen uncontrollably. She is seeking help with the hope of regaining some semblance of normalcy and finding ways to cope more effectively with her memories and triggers.
